# Why Bad News Sticks

Imagine you get ten compliments and one insult today. Which one will you still remember tonight? For most people, it's the insult. Psychologists call this the negativity bias.

## An Old Alarm

For our ancestors, missing a ripe berry cost a snack, but missing a lion cost everything. Brains that paid extra attention to danger survived. We inherited a brain that treats bad news as urgent.

## What It Does Today

Headlines with negative words get more clicks. Our brains are not broken. They are just tuned for a world with lions.
